title_en: Shanghai Hongkou District People's Procuratorate v. Chen Xinjin, Yu Mingjue, et al. — fraud case
ruling_gist_en: For the purpose of unlawfully taking possession of others' property, acts of fabricating "hospitals, experts, miracle drugs" and impersonating patients, medical guides, doctors, cashiers, medicine dispensers, etc., to defraud victims of their property shall be convicted and punished as the crime of fraud in accordance with Article 266 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China.
keywords_en: criminal; fraud; first instance; grassroots people's court; Shanghai; natural person; criminal law; elements of fraud; joint crime determination; determination of fraud amount; fabrication of expert identity; impersonating doctor to prescribe medicine; defrauding high medical fees
full_text_en:
Procuratorate of Hongkou District, Shanghai v. Chen Xinjin, Yu Mingjue, et al. — Fraud

[Ruling Summary]

Acts committed with the purpose of unlawfully appropriating another person's property, by fabricating a "hospital, experts, and miracle drugs," impersonating patients, medical guides, doctors, cashiers, drug dispensers, and other identities, to defraud victims of their property, shall be convicted and punished as the crime of fraud in accordance with the provisions of Article 266 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China.

Procuratorial Authority: Procuratorate of Hongkou District, Shanghai.

Defendants:

- Chen Xinjin, male, 57 years old, Han ethnicity, junior high school education, farmer. Detained on June 18, 2009, on suspicion of fraud; criminally detained on the following day; arrested on July 24, 2009.
- Yu Mingjue, male, 67 years old, Han ethnicity, college education, retired. Detained on June 18, 2009, on suspicion of fraud; criminally detained on the following day; arrested on July 24, 2009.
- Xiao Can, female, 20 years old, Han ethnicity, junior high school education, unemployed. Detained on June 18, 2009, on suspicion of fraud; criminally detained on the following day; arrested on July 24, 2009.
- Zuo Xinghua (formerly known as Zuo Xinhua), male, 41 years old, Han ethnicity, junior high school education, farmer. Detained on June 18, 2009, on suspicion of fraud; criminally detained on the following day; arrested on July 24, 2009.
- Zuo Yun'e, female, 47 years old, Han ethnicity, primary school education, farmer. Detained on June 18, 2009, on suspicion of fraud; criminally detained on the following day; arrested on July 24, 2009.
- Fan Yunhua, female, 35 years old, Han ethnicity, primary school education, farmer. Detained on June 18, 2009, on suspicion of fraud; criminally detained on the following day; arrested on July 24, 2009.

The Procuratorate of Hongkou District, Shanghai, initiated a public prosecution against the defendants Chen Xinjin, Yu Mingjue, Xiao Can, Zuo Xinghua, Zuo Yun'e, and Fan Yunhua for the crime of fraud before the Hongkou District People's Court of Shanghai.

The indictment alleged: The defendants Chen Xinjin, Yu Mingjue, Xiao Can, Zuo Xinghua, Zuo Yun'e, Fan Yunhua, together with Yi Dongliang, Tang Chungeng, Xie Xinwu (all separately prosecuted), and others, after prior conspiracy, formed a criminal fraud group. Between March and June 2009, at the Huaxia United Gene Health Detection Technology Service Center located on the 2nd floor of No. 30 Beihaining Road in this city, operated by Yi Dongliang, Tang Chungeng, and others, under the pretext of "treating illnesses," Chen Xinjin was fully responsible for the daily management of the center and arranged role assignments; Fan Yunhua and others were responsible for luring victims from reputable hospitals in Shanghai, including the Obstetrics and Gynecology Hospital Affiliated to Fudan University, Renji Hospital Affiliated to Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine, and Shanghai First People's Hospital, to the center for "treatment"; Zuo Yun'e was responsible for impersonating a medical guide on the first floor of the center, directing numerous victims to the consultation room on the second floor; Xiao Can was responsible for registration and fee collection; Yu Mingjue was responsible for impersonating "Professor Yu" to examine victims and write prescriptions; Zuo Xinghua and others were responsible for delivering medications to the center. They successively defrauded over 200 victims, including Cheng Ya, Zhang Guiying, and Shen Wunan, of exorbitant medication fees. Among them, the total defrauded amounts were: Chen Xinjin, Xiao Can, and Zuo Xinghua: RMB 539,822; Yu Mingjue: RMB 396,755; Zuo Yun'e: RMB 468,317; Fan Yunhua: RMB 24,225. The defendants Chen Xinjin, Yu Mingjue, Xiao Can, Zuo Xinghua, Zuo Yun'e, and Fan Yunhua, jointly with others, with the intent of illegal possession, used methods of fabricating facts and concealing the truth to defraud citizens of their property. The amounts defrauded by Chen Xinjin, Yu Mingjue, Xiao Can, Zuo Xinghua, and Zuo Yun'e were particularly huge; the amount defrauded by Fan Yunhua was relatively large. Therefore, they should all be held criminally liable for the crime of fraud in accordance with Article 266 and Article 25, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law of the PRC.

Defendants Zuo Xinghua and Fan Yunhua expressed no objection to the facts alleged in the indictment.

Defendant Chen Xinjin argued: Like the other defendants, he was hired by Yi Dongliang and Tang Chungeng at the end of February 2009 to work at the Huaxia United Gene Health Detection Technology Service Center, providing health consultations. He claimed the center prescribed medicine only at patients' requests, and patients could fill the prescriptions at outside pharmacies or have the service center help with dispensing. The purpose was to help patients treat illnesses, not to defraud them. He denied managing the center or assigning positions to the other defendants. He stated that the day's collected medication fees were allocated as follows: an 18% commission to the pharmacy managed by Tang Chungeng, a 55% commission to the "hospital tout" (yi tuo), a daily payment of RMB 110 to defendant Yu Mingjue for compensation and meals, and the remainder, after deducting daily expenses and wages for others, was temporarily held by him. He contested the indictment's claim of over 200 victims and an amount exceeding RMB 530,000, and noted that some fees had been refunded to victims after the fact. He also stated that he had returned to his hometown from May 8 to May 29, 2009, because his wife was ill and hospitalized, and thus was not connected to events at the center during that period.

Defendant Yu Mingjue argued: He originally worked as a factory doctor in another province and later retired. At the end of February 2009, he was introduced to work at the Huaxia United Gene Health Detection Technology Service Center, providing health consultations. He stated that others called him "Professor" or "Dr. Yu", but he never referred to himself as "Professor". He claimed he only wrote prescriptions at patients' requests and had no knowledge of where patients obtained their medicine or how much it cost. He stated he wrote only about 20 prescriptions and received RMB 110 daily from defendant Chen Xinjin for compensation and meals. He also mentioned he had returned to his hometown from the evening of May 18 to May 29, 2009, and argued that the indictment's allegation of over 200 victims and an amount of RMB 390,000 was insufficiently evidenced.

Defendant Xiao Can argued: She was introduced to work at the Huaxia United Gene Health Detection Technology Service Center at the end of February 2009. Defendant Chen Xinjin assigned her to handle registration and fee collection and to escort patients to "Dr. Yu" for consultation. She received her monthly salary, including for May, from Chen Xinjin. She admitted that after working for a month, she felt the center was abnormal, but claimed she did not know that Chen Xinjin and the others were defrauding people. She also stated she had left the service center from March 15 to April 25, 2009.

Defendant Zuo Yun'e argued: She started working at the Huaxia United Gene Health Detection Technology Service Center at the end of April 2009, assigned by defendant Chen Xinjin as a guide on the first floor. She returned to her hometown in mid-May, and after returning to Shanghai on June 3, she worked as a guide again until her arrest. She noted that defendant Fan Yunhua and others often brought patients to see the doctor and would ask her "Is Professor Yu in?" She knew that Fan Yunhua and the others were acting deliberately for the patients to see, but she still told Fan Yunhua, the others, and the patients that "Professor Yu" was on the second floor. She claimed she did not know that Chen Xinjin, Yu Mingjue, and the others were committing fraud. At the same time, Zuo Yun'e did not dispute the co-defendant Chen Xinjin's statement that he had paid her RMB 2,000 as wages for May in early June.

Defense counsel for defendant Chen Xinjin argued: Although the Huaxia United Gene Health Detection Technology Service Center did not hold a "Medical Institution Practice Permit," the defendant Yu Mingjue was once a doctor and had indeed taken the victims' pulses and treated them in this case. Therefore, the case should be treated as illegal medical practice. Counsel further argued that the amount of RMB 530,000 alleged by the prosecutorial authority as the defrauded sum involving Chen Xinjin was insufficiently evidenced, and that amounts refunded to some victims after they discovered the fraud should be deducted.

Defense counsel for defendant Yu Mingjue argued: Yu Mingjue had no subjective intent to commit fraud. He was recruited to work at the Huaxia United Gene Health Detection Technology Service Center, received daily compensation, did not share in the illicit proceeds, and had no prior conspiracy with defendant Chen Xinjin and others to commit fraud. Although others called Yu Mingjue "Professor," Yu Mingjue himself never claimed to be a "Professor" to the patients. Furthermore, Yu Mingjue had been a doctor and was qualified to treat patients. He was unaware of how Chen Xinjin and others were charging fees and dispensing drugs to defraud victims. Counsel also argued that the amount of RMB 390,000 alleged as the value of prescriptions written by Yu Mingjue was insufficiently evidenced.

Defense counsel for defendant Xiao Can argued: The evidence supporting the allegation that Xiao Can participated in defrauding RMB 530,000 was insufficient. Furthermore, some of the victims' illnesses could have been treated by defendant Yu Mingjue, and this amount should be deducted. Counsel also argued that Xiao Can played a secondary and auxiliary role in the crime and should be treated as an accessory. Noting that Xiao Can had a cooperative attitude after the incident, counsel recommended a mitigated punishment.

Defense counsel for defendant Fan Yunhua argued: Fan Yunhua was not an employee of the Huaxia United Gene Health Detection Technology Service Center and had no prior conspiracy with defendant Chen Xinjin and others to commit fraud. Fan Yunhua merely introduced patients for medical consultations, acting as a "hospital tout." Defense counsel contended that current law does not criminalize the act of being a "hospital tout." Additionally, Fan Yunhua was not the only person introducing patients to the service center for medical consultations, so the amount of fraud alleged against Fan Yunhua was insufficiently evidenced.

Facts Found by the First Instance Trial of Hongkou District People's Court of Shanghai:

Beginning in March 2009, defendant Chen Xinjin, at the Huaxia United Gene Health Detection Technology Service Center located on the 2nd floor of No. 30 Beihaining Road, Shanghai, which was established by Yi Dongliang, Tang Chungeng (both separately prosecuted), and others, together with Xie Mou (separately prosecuted) and others, assembled defendants Yu Mingjue, Xiao Can, Zuo Xinghua, Zuo Yun'e, Fan Yunhua, and others. Under the guise of "expert medical treatment," they used low-cost ordinary Chinese herbal medicines, misrepresented them as "specialty medications" for treating gynecological and other diseases, and by issuing "prescriptions," "dispensed" them to victims at exorbitant prices to defraud them of their money. Among them: Chen Xinjin was fully responsible for the daily management of the center, accounting, and distributing the illicit proceeds; Fan Yunhua and others, at the gates of the Obstetrics and Gynecology Hospital Affiliated to Fudan University, Renji Hospital Affiliated to Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine, and Shanghai First People's Hospital, after learning the victims' medical conditions, falsely claimed "I also had this disease and was cured by an expert; I'd like to introduce you to this expert for treatment." They thereby lured victims who originally intended to seek treatment at those hospitals to the Huaxia United Gene Health Detection Technology Service Center for "medical treatment." Zuo Yun'e was responsible for impersonating a medical guide on the first floor of the center, directing victims to the consultation room on the second floor; Xiao Can was responsible for registration and fee collection, and faxing the "prescriptions" to the "pharmacy"; Yu Mingjue pretended to be "Professor Yu" to examine victims and write "prescriptions"; Zuo Xinghua was responsible for delivering medicines to the center based on the prescriptions faxed by Xiao Can, and then retrieving medicines for Fan Yunhua and others. Up to June 18, 2009, the defendants in collusion successively defrauded 50 victims, including Cheng Ya, Zhang Guiying, and Shen Wunan, of exorbitant medication fees. The amounts involved were: Chen Xinjin, Xiao Can, and Zuo Xinghua: a total of RMB 166,386; Yu Mingjue: a total of RMB 105,166; Zuo Yun'e: a total of RMB 69,271. The victims Cheng Ya, Shen Wunan, Jian Xiujuan, Yang Xiaohui, Zhang Rong'e, Zhuang Chunyan, and Zhu Honghua were lured by Fan Yunhua to the above center for "medical treatment," with the defrauded amount totaling RMB 21,932.

On June 18, 2009, the defendants Chen Xinjin, Yu Mingjue, Xiao Can, Zuo Xinghua, Zuo Yun'e, and Fan Yunhua were arrested by public security officers at No. 30 Beihaining Road, this city. After the incident, the public security organs returned part of the seized illicit proceeds to victims Cheng Ya and Zhang Guiying.

The above facts are confirmed by evidence submitted by the prosecutorial authority, including: statements and partial identification transcripts from victims Cheng Ya, Zhang Guiying, Shen Wunan, Li Yanhua, Sheng Youzhen, Sun Cuiling, Xue Jingli, Hou Yinghui, Jian Xiujuan, Yang Xiaohui, Du Yunhua, Zhang Rong'e, He Lijun, Li Fangyong, Du Xuan, Zhuang Chunyan, Zhang Jinian, Zhou Yuli, Tao Airong, Huang Tianju, Gu Ting, Zhuo Haizhen, Zhu Honghua, Shen Ke, Yu Kemei, Zhang Wenjuan, Lin Manxiang, Yu Yan'er, Zhou Qingsong, Zhang Sanmao, Chen Aijuan, Yu Qiguan, Zhong Kun, Zhu Qingzhi, Jiang Xiaoli, Ding Chuye, Sheng Zhiyan, Zhang Xiaowen, Shen Sanmei, Gao Yingjie, Cao Guofeng, Wu Dejun, Xiao Saiyan, Chen Dongchun, Wu Liqin, Xuan Yaping, and others; testimony of witnesses Yi Dongliang and Tang Chungeng; identification transcripts of defendants Chen Xinjin, Yu Mingjue, Xiao Can, Zuo Xinghua, Zuo Yun'e, and Fan Yunhua; the "List of Evidence Seized" and "List of Seized and Returned Items" issued by the Hongkou Branch of the Shanghai Public Security Bureau; certificates issued by the Obstetrics and Gynecology Hospital Affiliated to Fudan University, Renji Hospital Affiliated to Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine, and Shanghai First People's Hospital; seized documentary evidence, including the consultation manual of the Huaxia United Gene Health Detection Technology Service Center, daily patient treatment registration forms, accounting records, prescription slips, and the lease agreement; the "Certificate of Verification of Uniform Invoices" issued by the Yangpu Branch of the Shanghai Local Taxation Bureau; the "Analysis and Appraisal of Some Prescribed Drugs" issued by the Drug Sales Branch of Shanghai Leiyunshang Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.; and the "Administrative Penalty Decision" issued by the Hongkou District Health Bureau of Shanghai. The above evidence has been examined in court, corroborates each other without contradiction, is conclusive and sufficient, and is hereby affirmed.

The disputed issues at first instance in this case were: (1) whether the conduct of inducing patients to attend a non-qualified health center and selling overpriced, poor-quality drugs constitutes a crime; and (2) how to determine the amount of the crime.

Opinion of the First Instance Trial of Hongkou District People's Court of Shanghai:

In this case, the defendants Chen Xinjin, Yu Mingjue, Xiao Can, Zuo Xinghua, Zuo Yun'e, Fan Yunhua, and others, in collusion, with the intent of illegal possession, used methods of fabricating facts and concealing the truth to defraud others of their property. The amounts defrauded by Chen Xinjin, Yu Mingjue, Xiao Can, Zuo Xinghua, and Zuo Yun'e were huge; the amount defrauded by defendant Fan Yunhua was relatively large. Their conduct has all constituted the crime of fraud. The charges by the Procuratorate of Hongkou District, Shanghai, against Chen Xinjin, Yu Mingjue, Xiao Can, Zuo Xinghua, Zuo Yun'e, and Fan Yunhua for the crime of fraud are established.

In their pursuit of financial gain, the defendants Chen Xinjin and others, knowing that defendant Yu Mingjue was neither a specialist in traditional Chinese medicine nor in possession of a physician's practice certificate, nonetheless assembled defendants Yu Mingjue, Xiao Can, Zuo Xinghua, Zuo Yun'e, Fan Yunhua, and others. Fan Yunhua fabricated facts to lure victims to the above-mentioned "center." Under the pretext of "medical treatment," they misrepresented low-cost ordinary Chinese herbal medicines as "specialty medications" and "dispensed" them to victims at exorbitant prices. Yu Mingjue, knowing that he did not hold a physician's practice certificate and was not permitted to engage in medical activities, and lacking any expertise in treating various specialized diseases, nonetheless, in order to obtain money, knowing that the victims had been deceived by "hospital touts" to come to him for "treatment," impersonated a "Professor." After merely brief questioning and taking the victims' pulses, he issued so-called "prescriptions" for specific specialty disease "miracle drugs." This led the victims to mistakenly believe they had received "treatment" from a specialist in traditional Chinese medicine. After the incident, all victims confirmed that taking the Chinese herbal medicines prescribed by Yu Mingjue and others resulted in no improvement in their illnesses, thereby proving that the "medicines" prescribed by Yu Mingjue were not appropriate treatments. Therefore, Chen Xinjin and Yu Mingjue had the subjective intent to commit fraud. Xiao Can, Zuo Xinghua, and Zuo Yun'e knew that the victims had been lured to the above-mentioned "center" by Fan Yunhua and others, and that the so-called "medical treatment" by Chen Xinjin, Yu Mingjue, and others was suspicious. Nonetheless, they created false impressions to help conceal the truth, demonstrating that Xiao Can, Zuo Xinghua, and Zuo Yun'e also had the subjective intent to commit fraud. Although Fan Yunhua was not employed by Chen Xinjin, she colluded with Chen Xinjin and others for financial gain. Knowing that Yu Mingjue and the others were not experts in traditional Chinese medicine, she nonetheless fabricated facts to lure victims to the above-mentioned "center" for "medical treatment" and subsequently received a high commission on the exorbitant medication fees. She had a subjective intent of illegal appropriation and objectively carried out acts of fabricating facts, which conforms to the constitutive elements of the crime of fraud and should be punished as such. Pursuant to Articles 336, 141, and 142 of the Criminal Law, the crime of illegal medical practice refers to conduct where a person without the qualification of a practicing physician engages in illegal medical practice under serious circumstances. The crime of manufacturing and selling counterfeit drugs refers to the manufacture or sale of counterfeit drugs that is sufficient to seriously endanger human health. The crime of manufacturing and selling inferior drugs refers to the manufacture or sale of inferior drugs that causes serious harm to human health. Based on the facts of this case, the conduct of the above defendants was, in essence, neither the practice of medicine nor the sale of medicine; the acts of "examining patients and selling drugs" they carried out were merely deceptive means used to commit the crime of fraud. Therefore, the defense arguments and submissions by the defense counsel for Chen Xinjin, Yu Mingjue, and Fan Yunhua, and by Chen Xinjin, Yu Mingjue, Xiao Can, and Zuo Yun'e regarding the characterization of the case cannot stand, and the court rejects them.

Regarding the defense arguments by defendants Chen Xinjin and Yu Mingjue and their respective defense counsel that the evidence was insufficient to establish the amounts of fraud attributed to each defendant, the court found upon investigation: The prosecutorial authority calculated the defrauded amounts and the number of victims based on the medication fee amounts recorded by Chen Xinjin and others in the daily patient treatment registration forms, and the period during which each defendant participated in the fraud at the Huaxia United Gene Health Detection Technology Service Center. Additionally, the prosecutorial authority determined the amount of fraud by defendant Fan Yunhua based on victims' identification transcripts. However, the evidence was not sufficiently conclusive. Therefore, the court accepts the aforementioned defense arguments by Chen Xinjin, Yu Mingjue, and their defense counsel. Based on the verified records of victims' statements, identification transcripts, Fan Yunhua's identification transcripts of victims, the seized and verified medication fee amounts for identified victims recorded by Chen Xinjin and others in the daily patient treatment registration forms, the seized partial "prescriptions," invoices, consultation manuals, and the periods during which each defendant participated in the fraud at the center, the court determined the amount of fraud attributable to each defendant.

Defendant Chen Xinjin argued that he had returned to his hometown in Hunan from May 8 to May 29, 2009, and therefore had no connection to the events that occurred at the Huaxia United Gene Health Testing Technology Service Center during that period. The court held that: The Huaxia United Gene Health Testing Technology Service Center was managed by Chen Xinjin, who was responsible for arranging the division of labor among the defendants, distributing the defrauded proceeds in the form of wages, and retaining the remaining funds. If Chen Xinjin wished to temporarily cease the criminal activity, he was required to effectively and completely prevent the occurrence of the criminal results. However, from May 8 to May 29, 2009, the defendants Yu Mingjue, Xiao Can, Zuo Xinghua, and others continued to commit fraud against outsiders in the name of the Huaxia United Gene Health Testing Technology Service Center. Xiao Can, Zuo Xinghua, and witnesses Yi Dongliang and Tang Chungeng all confirmed that the wages, commissions, and dividends for May were also distributed by Chen Xinjin. Therefore, whether Chen Xinjin temporarily returned to his hometown during the aforementioned period does not affect the determination of his legal liability for the amount of fraud committed by Yu Mingjue, Xiao Can, Zuo Xinghua, and others during that period. Accordingly, Chen Xinjin's above argument is not consistent with the law, and the court does not accept it. Yu Mingjue argued that he had returned to his hometown from the evening of May 18 to May 29, 2009, which was corroborated by corresponding evidence, and the prosecutorial authority did not charge or find that Yu Mingjue participated in the fraud during that period. Xiao Can argued that he had left the aforementioned "center" from March 15 to April 25, 2009. Upon investigation, the court found that none of the currently recognized victims were defrauded during that period. Therefore, Xiao Can's argument does not affect the determination of the amount of his fraud. Defendant Zuo Yun'e argued that she started working as a medical guide at the aforementioned "center" at the end of April 2009, returned to her hometown in mid-May, and after returning to Shanghai on June 3, continued to work as a medical guide at the "center" until her arrest. Upon investigation: Co-defendant Chen Xinjin confirmed during the trial that Zuo Yun'e's monthly remuneration was RMB 2,000, calculated on a daily basis and paid after a full month. He had paid Zuo Yun'e RMB 2,000 in early June 2009. Therefore, the court accepts Defendant Zuo Yun'e's argument and finds that she worked as a medical guide at the aforementioned "center" for that period.

In the joint crime, Defendants Chen Xinjin, Yu Mingjue, and Fan Yunhua played primary roles and are principals. Defendants Xiao Can, Zuo Xinghua, and Zuo Yun'e played secondary or auxiliary roles and are accessories, thus eligible for comparatively lighter or mitigated punishment. The court accepts the defense counsel's opinion that Xiao Can is an accessory. However, considering Xiao Can's role in the crime and the amount of fraud he participated in, Xiao Can may receive a lighter punishment. The court does not accept the defense counsel's opinion requesting a mitigated punishment for Xiao Can.

Accordingly, in accordance with Article 266, paragraph 1 of Article 25, paragraphs 1 and 4 of Article 26, Article 27, and Article 64 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, the Hongkou District People's Court of Shanghai rendered the following judgment on March 19, 2010:

1. Defendant Chen Xinjin is convicted of fraud and sentenced to eight years' imprisonment, and shall also be fined RMB 10,000.

2. Defendant Yu Mingjue is convicted of fraud and sentenced to five years and six months' imprisonment, and shall also be fined RMB 6,000.

3. Defendant Xiao Can is convicted of fraud and sentenced to five years and six months' imprisonment, and shall also be fined RMB 6,000.

4. Defendant Zuo Xinghua is convicted of fraud and sentenced to five years' imprisonment, and shall also be fined RMB 5,000.

5. Defendant Zuo Yun'e is convicted of fraud and sentenced to one year and six months' imprisonment, and shall also be fined RMB 2,000.

6. Defendant Fan Yunhua is convicted of fraud and sentenced to one year and three months' imprisonment, and shall also be fined RMB 2,000.

7. The defrauded proceeds shall be recovered and returned to the respective victims.

Chen Xinjin and Xiao Can, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Shanghai Second Intermediate People's Court. Appellant Chen Xinjin and his defense counsel argued that Chen Xinjin was not the principal who organized and led the joint fraud crime, and that Chen Xinjin should not be held responsible for all the criminal facts; that Chen Xinjin left Shanghai from May 8 to May 29, 2009, and did not participate in the fraudulent activities, and thus should not bear responsibility for the amount of fraud during that period. Appellant Xiao Can and his defense counsel argued that Xiao Can had been recruited through a job advertisement to work at the Huaxia United Gene Health Testing Technology Service Center, that Xiao Can was unaware that the center was engaged in fraudulent criminal activities, and that the evidence for the amount of fraud determined in the original judgment was insufficient.

Upon second-instance trial, the Shanghai Second Intermediate People's Court confirmed the facts found in the first instance.

The Shanghai Second Intermediate People's Court held in the second instance that:

This case constitutes a joint fraud crime, organized by principal members in the form of shares, carried out in the name of the Huaxia United Gene Health Testing Technology Service Center through illegal medical practice. Appellant Chen Xinjin, as one of the shareholders and responsible for the daily management of the center, directly organized other offenders to specifically implement the fraud against the victims' property. He shall be held responsible for all the criminal facts. Although Appellant Xiao Can was an employee of the center, he knew that the victims had been lured to the center by the original trial defendant Fan Yunhua and others, and that accomplices disguised as "patients" were present, allowing Yu Mingjue and others to perform so-called "medical treatment." Xiao Can assisted in this process, covering up the facts, indicating that Xiao Can also had subjective intent to commit fraud. The original judgment's determination of the amount of fraud based on the victims' statements, the accounting records made by Chen Xinjin and others, and the seized partial prescriptions and invoices, among other evidence, was not improper. The original judgment's finding that Chen Xinjin, Xiao Can, and the original trial defendants Yu Mingjue, Zuo Xinghua, Zuo Yun'e, and Fan Yunhua were guilty of fraud was based on clear facts, reliable and sufficient evidence, correct application of the law, appropriate sentencing, and lawful trial procedures.

Accordingly, in accordance with Article 189, paragraph (1) of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Shanghai Second Intermediate People's Court ruled on June 1, 2010:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

This ruling is final.
